problem: Existing VLA navigation models (UniNavid, StreamVLN, Nav-R1) use single-turn imitation learning or single-turn GRPO-style RL, so they ignore sequential causal dependencies, imitate rigid human demos, and fail on long-horizon episodes. Critic-free RL (GRPO, REINFORCE++) uses horizon-agnostic outcome baselines, while PPO critics are too costly for long sequences.
motivation: Navigation spans hundreds of steps where early exploration determines late efficiency, so temporal credit assignment matters. Online RL can discover diverse behaviors beyond demonstrations. A cheap critic-free baseline that is aware of time/horizon is needed for large VLAs.
key_idea: Cast navigation as a multi-turn conversation with a KV-cached VLA trained with online RL, using HAPO, a critic-free advantage estimator whose baseline is a leave-one-out Gaussian temporal-kernel regression over rollout returns.
insight: Dense step-level rewards plus a time-aware baseline are what make RL beat SFT: REINFORCE++ with sparse outcome reward (47.4 SR) is worse than SFT (64.3), while HAPO reaches 73.0. Restricting the kernel bandwidth (sigma=30 vs infinity) lowers value error on >200-step episodes and lifts SR from 0 to 15.4 there, with identical performance on short ones. Timestep as kernel feature beats per-trajectory and distance features (76.4 vs 71.0/73.4 SR).
method: Multi-turn VLA formulation: policy conditions on instruction, full history of observations and actions via KV cache, so each step is a turn; cache reuse makes hundreds of steps tractable
Online token pruning: drop current-frame visual tokens whose max similarity to cached keys exceeds threshold delta (e.g. 0.95-0.97), cutting time/memory with a causal, single-pass training

HAPO advantage: A=G-V, where V is leave-one-out Gaussian kernel regression over timestep feature (sigma=30) across a buffer of the last 256 trajectories; REINFORCE++ is the constant-kernel special case
Dense reward: -Δgeodesic distance -0.01 per step plus terminal 2.5·SPL; gamma=0.95
Balanced IL warm-up: SFT with LoRA on Habitat-Web demonstrations with uniform sampling over trajectory lengths 0-400 to remove stop-length bias (64.3 SR at 30k)

Online RL: dual-clip PPO objective with global-batch advantage normalization, ClipCov entropy control, full KL to SFT reference (coef 0.001), asynchronous rollout workers, ~4000 episodes, 350-step cap

setting.training_data: Habitat-Web human demos (up to 30k uniformly sampled trajectories, truncated to 500 steps) for SFT; then ~4k online RL episodes on 80 HM3D training scenes (6 object categories)
setting.action_space: discrete: MOVE FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN LEFT/RIGHT 30°, STOP
setting.privileged: none at test time (geodesic distance reward used only in training)

results: LongNav-R1 (RGB-only, 2B) reaches SR 76.0/83.7/63.0 on HM3D V1/V2/MP3D, beating UniNavid (73.7 SR, 37.1 SPL on V1) and PIRLNav-RL (70.4). On OVON val-unseen it gets 53.8 SR zero-shot versus Nav-R1 42.2 and MTU3D 40.8. RL adds 8.7 SR over the 64.3 SFT warm-up with only ~4k episodes.
limitations: Full KV cache is retained, so memory still grows in extreme-horizon tasks; performance drops after ~150 steps and long (>200-step) success remains low (15.4)
